recipes.title: Cucumber with Plant-Based Yogurt and Mint
recipes.sourceText: Recipe n°1  Cucumber with Plant-Based Yogurt and Mint  Health Goal  Provide digestive freshness, hydration, and lightness. Ideal for soothing inflammation and supporting the microbiota.  Servings  2 people  Ingredients     1 large fresh cucumber     150 g plain plant-based yogurt (soy or coconut)     1 handful of fresh mint leaves     1 tbsp extra virgin olive oil     1 pinch of sea salt     A squeeze of lemon juice  Preparation  1)   Wash and peel the cucumber, then slice it into thin rounds.  2)   Chop the mint finely.  3)   Mix the plant-based yogurt with olive oil, lemon juice, and salt.  4)   Add the cucumber slices and mint, and mix gently.  5)   Serve well chilled.  Time  Preparation: 10 min  Rest: 15 min in the fridge  Benefits     Cucumber: hydrating, rich in minerals.     Plant-based yogurt: gentle source of probiotics.     Mint: soothing for digestion.     Lemon: boosts immunity and vitality.  Tip  Add a few pumpkin or sunflower seeds for extra protein and crunch.  Variation  Replace mint with coriander for an oriental touch.  Nutrition  Hypotoxic recipe, gluten-free and dairy-free, light and refreshing.  41

recipes.title: Raw Turnip with Ginger and Coriander
recipes.sourceText: Recipe n°11  Raw Turnip with Ginger and Coriander  Health Goal  Provide freshness, fiber, and digestive tone. Ideal for boosting vitality and supporting the immune system.  Servings  2 people  Ingredients     2 small fresh turnips     1 tsp freshly grated ginger     1 small bunch of fresh coriander     Juice of half a lemon     1 tbsp extra virgin olive oil     1 pinch of sea salt  Preparation  1)   Wash and peel the turnips.  2)   Grate them finely or slice into thin strips.  3)   Mix with ginger, lemon juice, and olive oil.  4)   Add chopped coriander and salt.  5)   Serve immediately to preserve freshness.  Time  Preparation: 10 min  Benefits     Turnip: rich in fiber and antioxidants, light and remineralizing.     Ginger: digestive stimulant and anti-inflammatory.     Coriander: detoxifying and refreshing.     Lemon: invigorating and high in vitamin C.     Olive oil: protective for the heart and cells.  Tip  Add a few sesame seeds for extra crunch and mineral intake.  Variation  Replace coriander with mint for a milder flavor.  Nutrition  Hypotoxic recipe, gluten-free and dairy-free, rich in fiber and antioxidants.  55

recipes.title: Warm quinoa with green vegetables
recipes.sourceText: Recipe no. 21  Warm quinoa with green vegetables  Health goal  Provide plant-based proteins, fiber, and antioxidants. Ideal for supporting energy and digestive balance.  Servings  2 people  Ingredients     100 g quinoa     1 small zucchini     1 handful of green beans     1 handful of arugula     1 tbsp extra virgin olive oil     Juice of half a lemon     A pinch of sea salt  Preparation  1)   Rinse the quinoa and cook for 12 minutes in twice its volume of water.  2)   Drain and let cool slightly.  3)   Steam the green beans lightly (keep them crunchy).  4)   Cut the zucchini into small cubes, raw or lightly blanched.  5)   Mix the quinoa with the vegetables, olive oil, lemon juice, and salt.  6)   Add the arugula just before serving.  Time  Preparation: 10 min  Cooking: 12 min  Benefits     Quinoa: rich in complete proteins and minerals.     Green beans: source of fiber and vitamin C.     Zucchini: hydrating and light.     Arugula: antioxidant and stimulating.     Olive oil: protective for the heart and cells.  Tip  Add a few sunflower seeds for extra crunch.  Variation  Replace arugula with parsley for a milder flavor.  Nutrition  Hypotoxic recipe, gluten-free and dairy-free, rich in plant proteins and fiber.  69

recipes.title: Fennel with Orange and Olive Oil
recipes.sourceText: Recipe No. 31  Fennel with Orange and Olive Oil  Health Objective  Provide fiber, vitamin C, and digestive freshness. Ideal for supporting immunity and easing digestion.  Servings  2 people  Ingredients     1 fresh fennel bulb     1 orange (flesh + juice)     1 tbsp virgin olive oil     A pinch of sea salt  Preparation  1)   Wash and finely slice the fennel.  2)   Peel the orange and cut the flesh into small pieces.  3)   Mix the fennel with the orange and its juice.  4)   Add olive oil and salt.  5)   Serve fresh.  Time  Preparation: 10 minutes  Benefits     Fennel: digestive, rich in fiber and minerals.     Orange: source of vitamin C and antioxidants.     Olive oil: protective for the heart and cells.  Tip  Add a few sunflower seeds to enhance crunchiness.  Variation  Replace the orange with grapefruit for a more tangy flavor.  Nutrition  Hypotoxic recipe, gluten-free and dairy-free, rich in fiber and antioxidants.  83

recipes.title: Roasted Butternut Squash with Zaatar and Lemon
recipes.sourceText: Recipe No. 41  Roasted Butternut Squash with Zaatar and Lemon  Health Objective  Provide fiber, antioxidants, and support digestion.  Servings  2 people  Ingredients     1 small butternut squash     1 tbsp extra virgin olive oil     1 tsp zaatar     Juice of half a lemon     Sea salt  Preparation  1)   Peel and cut the squash into cubes.  2)   Mix with olive oil, salt, and zaatar.  3)   Roast in the oven at 180°C (350°F) for 25 minutes.  4)   Drizzle with lemon juice before serving.  Time  Preparation: 10 minutes Cooking: 25 minutes  Benefits     Butternut squash: rich in beta-carotene, supports vision and immunity.     Zaatar: blend of antioxidant herbs.     Lemon: boosts vitamin C.     Olive oil: protects the heart.  Tip  Add a few pomegranate seeds for a sweet and colorful touch.  Variation  Replace zaatar with fresh thyme.  Nutrition  Hypotoxic recipe, gluten-free and dairy-free, rich in fiber and antioxidants.  97

recipes.title: Green Lentil Cream with Ginger
recipes.sourceText: Recipe n°51  Green Lentil Cream with Ginger  Health Goal  Soothing and rich in fiber, this cream supports digestion and provides plant-based proteins.  Servings  2 people  Ingredients     150 g green lentils     1 carrot     1 piece of fresh ginger (2 cm)     500 ml water or vegetable broth     1 tbsp olive oil     Sea salt, pepper  Preparation  1)   Rinse the lentils.  2)   Dice the carrot and grate the ginger.  3)   Cook lentils + carrot + ginger in water for 25 minutes.  4)   Blend with olive oil, adjust seasoning.  Time  Preparation: 10 min  Cooking: 25 min  Benefits     Complete plant-based proteins     Fiber for satiety     Ginger: gentle anti-inflammatory effect  Tip  Add a splash of lemon juice to enhance flavor.  Variation  Replace green lentils with blonde lentils.  Nutrition  Hypotoxic recipe, gluten-free and dairy-free, rich in plant-based proteins, fiber, and antioxidants.  115

recipes.title: Zucchini Soup with Basil and Lemon
recipes.sourceText: Recipe No. 61  Zucchini Soup with Basil and Lemon  Health Objective  Light and refreshing, this soup promotes digestion and provides protective antioxidants.  Servings  2 people  Ingredients  •   2 medium zucchinis  •   1 handful of fresh basil  •   Juice of half a lemon  •   500 ml water or vegetable broth  •   1 tbsp olive oil  •   Sea salt, pepper  Preparation  1)   Wash and slice the zucchinis.  2)   Cook in water or broth for 15 minutes.  3)   Blend with basil, lemon juice, and olive oil.  4)   Season to taste.  Time  Preparation: 10 min  Cooking: 15 min  Benefits  •   Zucchini: rich in gentle fiber and minerals  •   Basil: digestive properties and fresh flavor  •   Lemon: vitamin C and detoxifying effect  Tip  Add some lemon zest to intensify freshness.  Variation  Replace basil with fresh mint.  Nutrition  Hypotoxic recipe, gluten-free and dairy-free, rich in fiber, vitamin C, and antioxidants.  129

recipes.title: Green Lentil Soup with Coriander
recipes.sourceText: Recipe No. 71  Green Lentil Soup with Coriander  Health Objective  Rich in plant proteins and fiber, this soup supports energy and promotes digestion.  Servings  2 people  Ingredients  •   150 g green lentils  •   1 carrot  •   1 garlic clove  •   1 handful of fresh coriander  •   600 ml water or vegetable broth  •   1 tbsp olive oil  •   Sea salt, pepper  Preparation  1)   Rinse the green lentils.  2)   Dice the carrot and chop the garlic.  3)   Cook lentils + carrot + garlic in water for 25 minutes.  4)   Blend with coriander and olive oil.  5)   Season to taste.  Time  Preparation: 10 min  Cooking: 25 min  Benefits  •   Green lentils: plant proteins, iron, and fiber  •   Coriander: digestive and detoxifying effect  •   Nourishing and balanced dish  Tip  Add a pinch of cumin to enhance the flavor.  Variation  Replace coriander with flat-leaf parsley.  Nutrition  Hypotoxic recipe, gluten-free and dairy-free, rich in plant proteins, fiber, and minerals.  143

recipes.title: Vegetable Broth with Garlic and Parsley
recipes.sourceText: Recipe No. 81  Vegetable Broth with Garlic and Parsley  Health Objective  Light and remineralizing, this broth promotes digestion and supports immunity thanks to garlic and parsley.  Servings  2 people  Ingredients  •   1 carrot  •   1 zucchini  •   1 celery stalk  •   1 garlic clove  •   1 handful of fresh parsley  •   700 ml water  •   Sea salt, pepper  Preparation  1)   Wash and cut the vegetables into pieces.  2)   Cook in water with garlic for 20 minutes.  3)   Add parsley at the end of cooking.  4)   Serve hot, filtered or with pieces.  Time  Preparation: 10 min  Cooking: 20 min  Benefits  •   Vegetables: source of fiber and minerals  •   Garlic: antimicrobial and stimulating properties  •   Parsley: rich in vitamin C and iron  Tip  Add a few fennel seeds to enhance the digestive effect.  Variation  Replace parsley with fresh coriander.  Nutrition  Hypotoxic recipe, gluten-free and dairy-free, rich in minerals and antioxidants.  157

recipes.title: Sweet Potato Purée with Cinnamon
recipes.sourceText: Recipe No. 91  Sweet Potato Purée with Cinnamon  Health Goal  Comforting and gentle, this purée provides energy and antioxidants while supporting digestion.  Servings  2 people  Ingredients  •   250 g sweet potato  •   1 tsp ground cinnamon  •   1 tbsp olive oil or plant-based milk (optional)  •   Sea salt  Preparation  1)   Peel and dice the sweet potato.  2)   Steam or boil for 20 minutes.  3)   Mash into a purée with cinnamon and olive oil.  4)   Season lightly.  Time  Preparation: 10 min  Cooking: 20 min  Benefits  •   Sweet potato: rich in fiber and beta-carotene  •   Cinnamon: supports glycemic regulation and offers a warm aroma  Tip  Add a splash of lemon juice to intensify freshness.  Variation  Replace cinnamon with ginger for a more tonic flavor.  Nutrition  Hypotoxic recipe, gluten-free and dairy-free, rich in fiber and antioxidants.  171

recipes.title: Pageot in Papillote with Lemon and Parsley
recipes.sourceText: Recipe No. 101  Pageot in Papillote with Lemon and Parsley  Health Goal  Hypotoxic dish rich in lean protein and beneficial fatty acids, supporting light digestion and cardiovascular protection.  Servings  2 people  Ingredients  •   2 fresh pageot fillets  •   1 lemon (juice + a few thin slices)  •   1 tbsp extra-virgin olive oil  •   1 small garlic clove, crushed  •   1 handful fresh parsley, chopped  •   Sea salt and mild pepper  Preparation  1)   Preheat the oven to 180 °C.  2)   Place each pageot fillet on a sheet of baking paper.  3)   Drizzle with lemon juice, add slices, garlic, and parsley.  4)   Season lightly, then close the papillote.  5)   Bake for 20 minutes.  Time  Preparation: 10 min  Cooking: 20 min  Benefits  •   Source of lean protein, easy to digest  •   Lemon and parsley rich in antioxidants and vitamin C  •   Papillote cooking preserves nutrients and limits fat  Tip  Add a few fennel seeds to enhance digestive freshness.  Variation  Replace parsley with coriander for a more oriental touch.  Nutrition  This dish provides a good amount of high-quality protein, essential for muscle maintenance and daily vitality. Overall, it is a light, balanced, and protective meal.  197

recipes.title: Chargou (Sar) Tajine with Vegetables and Coriander
recipes.sourceText: Recipe No. 111  Chargou (Sar) Tajine with Vegetables and Coriander  Health Goal  A complete hypotoxic dish, rich in protein and fiber, that supports digestion and vitality.  Servings  4 people  Ingredients  •   500 g fresh Chargou (Sar), cut into pieces  •   2 carrots, sliced  •   1 zucchini, diced  •   1 red bell pepper, cut into strips  •   1 peeled tomato, chopped  •   2 tbsp extra-virgin olive oil  •   1 garlic clove, crushed  •   1 tsp cumin  •   1 handful fresh coriander, chopped  •   Sea salt and mild pepper  Preparation  1)   In a tajine or casserole, heat olive oil and garlic.  2)   Add vegetables and spices, simmer for 10 minutes.  3)   Place the Chargou pieces on top of the vegetables.  4)   Cover and cook gently for 25 minutes.  5)   Sprinkle with fresh coriander before serving.  Time  Preparation: 15 min  Cooking: 35 min  Benefits  •   Chargou provides lean, easily digestible protein.  •   Vegetables enrich the dish with fiber, vitamins, and antioxidants.  •   Coriander supports digestion and adds freshness.  Tip  Add a few green olives to enhance the Mediterranean flavor.  Variation  Replace zucchini with turnip for a more traditional touch.  Nutrition  This tajine provides high-quality protein that nourishes without weighing down. Vegetables add fiber and antioxidants, supporting digestion and cellular protection.  211

recipes.title: Hard-Boiled Eggs with Cumin and Fresh Parsley
recipes.sourceText: Recipe n°121  Hard-Boiled Eggs with Cumin and Fresh Parsley  Health Objective  A hypotoxic snack rich in protein and antioxidants, supporting satiety and digestion.  Servings  2 people  Ingredients     4   organic eggs     1 tsp ground cumin     1 handful fresh parsley, chopped     Sea salt and mild pepper     A drizzle of extra virgin olive oil  Preparation  1)   Cook the eggs in boiling water for 10 minutes.  2)   Cool them, peel, and cut in half.  3)   Sprinkle with cumin and fresh parsley.  4)   Drizzle with olive oil before serving.  Time  Preparation: 5 min  Cooking: 10 min  Benefits     Eggs provide complete, easily digestible protein.     Cumin stimulates digestion and reduces bloating.     Parsley adds vitamin C and protective antioxidants.  Tip  Serve with cucumber slices for extra freshness.  Variation  Replace cumin with sweet paprika for a different flavor.  Nutrition  This recipe delivers high-quality protein that promotes satiety and energy. Overall, it is a simple, balanced, and protective preparation.  231

recipes.title: Poached Eggs with Lentils and Cilantro
recipes.sourceText: Recipe No. 131  Poached Eggs with Lentils and Cilantro  Health Objective  A hypotoxic dish rich in both plant and animal proteins, promoting satiety and supporting digestion.  Servings  2 people  Ingredients     4 organic eggs     150 g cooked green lentils     1 clove garlic, crushed     1 tbsp extra virgin olive oil     Juice of half a lemon     1 handful fresh cilantro, chopped     Sea salt and mild pepper  Preparation  1)   Cook the lentils in lightly salted water until tender.  2)   Drain and season with garlic, olive oil, and lemon juice.  3)   Poach the eggs in simmering water for 3 minutes.  4)   Arrange the poached eggs on the bed of lentils.  5)   Sprinkle with fresh cilantro before serving.  Time  Preparation: 10 min  Cooking: 20 min  Benefits     Eggs provide complete, easily digestible proteins.     Lentils are rich in fiber and protective minerals.     Cilantro supports digestion and adds freshness.  Tip  Add a pinch of cumin to enhance flavor and digestive effect.  Variation  Replace green lentils with red lentils for a softer texture.  Nutrition  This dish combines animal and plant proteins, promoting satiety and nutritional balance. Overall, it is a balanced, nourishing, and protective preparation.  245

recipes.title: Chicken en Papillote with Lemon and Thyme
recipes.sourceText: Recipe No. 141  Chicken en Papillote with Lemon and Thyme  Health Objective  A light and fragrant hypotoxic dish, rich in lean protein and antioxidants, that supports digestion and immunity.  Servings  2 people  Ingredients     2 free-range chicken breasts     1 organic lemon (slices + juice)     4 sprigs of fresh thyme     1 tbsp extra virgin olive oil     Sea salt and mild pepper  Preparation  1)   Preheat the oven to 160 °C (320 °F).  2)   Place each chicken breast on a sheet of parchment paper.  3)   Add lemon slices, thyme, and drizzle with olive oil.  4)   Close the papillote and bake for 25 minutes.  5)   Serve hot with a drizzle of fresh lemon juice.  Time  Preparation: 5 min  Cooking: 25 min  Benefits     Chicken provides lean, easily digestible protein.     Lemon stimulates detoxification and strengthens immunity.     Thyme has antiseptic and digestive properties.  Tip  Add a pinch of cumin for a warm Moroccan touch.  Variation  Replace thyme with fresh coriander for a more local flavor.  Nutrition  A dish rich in high-quality protein, low in saturated fat. Should be limited in cases of egg intolerance or cholesterol-free diets.  265

recipes.title: Stewed Beef with Chickpeas and Cumin
recipes.sourceText: Recipe No. 151  Stewed Beef with Chickpeas and Cumin  Health Goal  A nourishing and balanced hypotoxic dish, rich in protein and fiber, supporting digestion and long-lasting energy.  Servings  4 people  Ingredients     600 g lean beef pieces (shank or chuck)     200 g cooked chickpeas     2 ripe tomatoes, diced     1 mild onion, sliced     1 tsp ground cumin     1 tbsp extra virgin olive oil     Sea salt and mild pepper     A few sprigs of fresh coriander  Preparation  1)   Sauté the onion and beef pieces in olive oil over low heat.  2)   Add the tomatoes, chickpeas, and sprinkle with cumin.  3)   Cover with a glass of water and simmer gently for 1 hour.  4)   Garnish with fresh coriander before serving.  Time  Preparation: 10 min  Cooking: 1 h  Benefits     Beef provides complete proteins and iron.     Chickpeas are rich in fiber and plant-based protein.     Cumin supports digestion and adds a warm flavor.  Tip  Add a few carrots to enrich fiber content and color.  Variation  Replace beef with veal for a milder version.  Nutrition  A complete dish, rich in both animal and plant proteins, with a high fiber intake. Chickpeas promote satiety and intestinal balance, while cumin and coriander enhance digestion and immunity.  .  279

recipes.title: Chickpea Flatbreads with Cumin
recipes.sourceText: Recipe No. 161  Chickpea Flatbreads with Cumin  Health Goal  A hypotoxic alternative to bread, rich in plant-based protein and fiber, supporting digestion and satiety.  Servings  4 flatbreads  Ingredients     200 g chickpea flour     1 tsp ground cumin     1 tbsp extra virgin olive oil     200 ml warm water     Sea salt  Preparation  1)   Mix the chickpea flour with cumin and salt.  2)   Gradually add water to form a soft dough.  3)   Shape into flatbreads and cook in a pan with a drizzle of olive oil, 3 minutes on each side.  Time  Preparation: 5 min  Cooking: 6 min  Benefits     Chickpeas provide plant-based protein and digestive fiber.     Cumin supports digestion and adds a warm flavor.     Olive oil enhances the intake of protective fatty acids.  Tip  Serve with a green salad or vegetable dip for a complete meal.  Variation  Add fresh chopped parsley for extra aromatic flavor.  Nutrition  Flatbreads rich in plant-based protein, fiber, and antioxidants - ideal as a bread substitute in a hypotoxic diet.  299

recipes.title: Sweet Potato Cream with Coconut Milk
recipes.sourceText: Recipe No. 171  Sweet Potato Cream with Coconut Milk  Health Objective  A gentle, comforting dessert, rich in fiber, beta-carotene, and protective fatty acids - ideal for sensitive digestive profiles.  Servings  4 small glasses  Ingredients     300 g cooked sweet potato     200 ml coconut milk     1 tsp cinnamon     1 tbsp date syrup (optional)  Preparation  1)   Blend the sweet potato with coconut milk until smooth and creamy.  2)   Add cinnamon and date syrup, then blend again.  3)   Pour into small glasses and refrigerate for 1 hour before serving.  Time  Preparation: 10 min  Rest: 1 h  Benefits     Sweet potato is high in fiber and beta-carotene.     Coconut milk provides protective fatty acids.     Cinnamon supports digestion and helps balance blood sugar.  Tip  Sprinkle with shredded coconut or chia seeds for added texture.  Variation  Replace cinnamon with vanilla or ginger to suit your taste.  Nutrition  A soft, nourishing cream - gluten-free and dairy-free - perfect for hypotoxic and sensitive digestive profiles.  319

recipes.title: Fresh Fruit Salad with Basil
recipes.sourceText: Recipe No. 181  Fresh Fruit Salad with Basil  Health Objective  A refreshing, vitamin-rich dessert, full of antioxidants and fiber - supporting hydration and vitality.  Servings  4 bowls  Ingredients     2 apples     2 pears     2 oranges     1 banana     1 handful of strawberries     A few fresh basil leaves     Juice of half a lemon  Preparation  1)   Wash and cut the fruits into pieces.  2)   Drizzle with lemon juice to prevent oxidation.  3)   Finely chop the basil and add to the fruits.  4)   Mix gently and serve fresh.  Time  Preparation: 10 min  Benefits     Fruits provide vitamins, fiber, and protective antioxidants.     Basil supports digestion and adds aromatic freshness.     A light, gluten-free, dairy-free dessert perfectly suited to hypotoxic profiles.  Tip  Add a few pomegranate seeds for extra color and vitality.  Variation  Replace basil with mint for a fresher flavor.  Nutrition  A salad rich in vitamin C and fiber - ideal for energy and digestive balance.  .  339

recipes.title: Carrot and Ginger Juice
recipes.sourceText: Recipe No. 191  Carrot and Ginger Juice  Health Goal  A tonic and protective juice, rich in beta-carotene and antioxidants, supporting vision and immunity.  Servings  2 large glasses  Ingredients     4 fresh carrots     1 small piece of fresh ginger (2 cm)     Juice of half a lemon (optional)  Preparation  1)   Wash and cut the carrots into pieces.  2)   Run the carrots and ginger through a juicer.  3)   Add the lemon juice for extra freshness.  4)   Serve immediately.  Time  Preparation: 10 minutes  Benefits     Carrots provide beta-carotene and protective fibers.     Ginger stimulates digestion and strengthens immunity.     Light, hypotoxic juice, gluten-free and dairy-free.  Tip  Add a pinch of turmeric to boost the antioxidant effect.  Variation  Replace ginger with mint for a milder flavor.  Nutrition  Juice rich in beta-carotene, vitamin C, and antioxidants, ideal for daily vitality.  359
